rationale: Full three-lens re-review (blind, edge-case, acceptance) of the unchanged EPMCDME-14138 diff, auditing against the ticket's acceptance criteria extracted from technical-analysis.md. All 6 business-review rows pass and standards checks (commit-format, code-quality, security) pass. Blind and edge-case independently raised a shared-workspace concurrency concern in AgentWorkspaceService.create_workspace, merged into CR-001 (patch, major). On follow-up investigation while applying the fix, the original finding's premise was corrected: a DB-level unique constraint on (conversation_id, user_id) already exists (uq_agent_workspaces_conversation_user, migration u1v2w3x4y5z6, pre-dating this diff), so the race could never have produced duplicate workspaces or lost file visibility as first claimed — the real gap was that create_workspace let a genuine constraint violation surface as an unhandled IntegrityError instead of resolving gracefully. That gap is now fixed (see CR-001 resolution); no schema migration was needed. 9 other raised observations were dismissed after verification: no-opt-out is the ticket's intended, accepted behavior (captured via the breaking-change risk flag, not a defect); the execution_id-uniqueness assumption and the str type annotation are pre-existing, already relied on by the existing MCP path (tool_node.py's _execute_mcp_tool already passes conversation_id=self.execution_id); the claimed asymmetry with the get_core_tools path was refuted by reading toolkit_service.py (that path never touches AgentWorkspace/AssistantChatRequest); the falsy-execution_id fallback is the tested, intended backward-compatibility behavior; workspace lifecycle/cleanup is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff; the test-helper-duplicates-production-lambda and missing-inline-comment points are non-blocking maintainability/documentation nits with no documented project rule making them blocking. No decision_needed findings, no defer findings, no findings remain unresolved.

findings.title: create_workspace did not handle the concurrent-creation race gracefully
findings.problem: create_workspace (agent_workspace_service.py:82-92, pre-fix) did check-then-insert (get_by_conversation_for_user, then save_workspace) with no handling for a concurrent collision. Correction to the original finding: a DB-level unique constraint on (conversation_id, user_id) already exists (uq_agent_workspaces_conversation_user, migration u1v2w3x4y5z6, pre-dating and unrelated to this diff), so a race could never create duplicate rows or silently lose file visibility as the original finding claimed — it would instead raise an unhandled IntegrityError out of create_workspace. Before this diff each bare tool state received its own random conversation_id, so two calls could never collide on the same key; this diff sets conversation_id=execution_id for every bare tool state in one workflow execution, so if a workflow can ever invoke bare tool states concurrently within the same execution, two calls could now hit that constraint for the first time.
findings.impact: A genuine concurrent collision on (conversation_id, user_id) would surface as an unhandled 500 (IntegrityError) instead of both callers resolving to the same workspace. Data integrity itself was never at risk (the constraint already guarantees no duplicate rows); this was a resilience/UX gap, not data loss.
findings.recommendation: Catch the IntegrityError in create_workspace and re-fetch/return the existing workspace on conflict, matching the codebase's existing pattern (see repository/user_kata_progress_repository.py's start_kata). No new migration needed — the constraint already exists.
findings.resolution: Fixed in agent_workspace_service.py: create_workspace now catches sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError around the insert and re-fetches the winning row via get_by_conversation_for_user before proceeding, instead of letting the exception propagate.
